title: Why he loves Dick Gibson's jazz party
summary: He praises the party's closeness and organization, with Gibson improvising set combinations such as Faddis and Eubie Blake.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Stanley and Helen were both at Dick Gibson's right?
Yeah, they were there, uh-huh. Have you ever been up there?
I've heard a lot of great things about it.

Well, it's a lot of -- it's different from probably any of those things you'll ever see. It's altogether different, you know. You're so close to the guys because, you know, it's one of those things. And, you know, you don't need no guards or nothing backstage or nothing. You know, everybody's just mingling, you know. And it's real close. And the guy who runs it is real good, you know. It comes off real good the way he does it. And there ain't no dull spots. It's going all the time and it's smooth, you know, the way it's going.

I like the way he does it. I like the way he treats people, you know. I'm not saying that the others don't treat them all right but the ones I've played, it's been a little too much protocol, you know. You can't walk backstage and see guys and things like this, and there ain't no backstage to walk here, you know. You're just in a spot and everybody's close together, you know.
It is. It's just what he said. It's not

a festival. It's a party and it's fun. I really enjoy it. I really get a big bang out of doing it, you know. It's -- I think everybody that goes there feels the same way. It isn't like you're going to make a couple of bucks somewhere. You don't even think about it from that point of view. You just -- the guy just treats you so nice. And one thing I really enjoy about him is you'll always know what you're doing.

Some of them I've been on actually it's so -- they're so haphazard. Nobody ever doesn't seem to know what they're doing, when they're doing it or what. But this thing you know exactly what you're doing. Now, he might improvise and switch which is good, and switch things around a little bit. Sometimes he might say, oh, I think I'll put on four trombones and a rhythm section right here this time, and it works. He does it, you know. Say let's play a few numbers, two or three songs together before we bring the next group out. And it works. It's beautiful like that. Yeah, you know where you're at all the time.
And he shocked everybody when he brought out Faddis and -- Jon Faddis. Can you imagine that? And Eubie Blake. 22 and 94. He should name that number 2294.
Yeah, he should do it. It was fun. I'm going to let you go now.
